Synopsis: A Taiwanese family fractures after their rebellious younger son is imprisoned for a violent assault, forcing a stoic, emotionally withdrawn father and his devoted wife to confront their sharply different capacities for forgiveness and love. The film unfolds over several years, tracing the long shadows that one act of violence casts across the entire family.

Title: Agent Sai Srinivasa Athreya
Synopsis: A self-styled, earnest Telugu detective running a struggling agency in a small town takes on what appears to be a routine missing-persons case, only to find himself drawn into a much more sinister conspiracy. The film blends sharp comedy with genre-savvy mystery plotting, affectionately riffing on classic detective fiction tropes.

Title: Asuran
Synopsis: When a violent confrontation with an oppressive upper-caste landlord sparks a retaliatory act by his defiant son, a mild-mannered Tamil farmer must summon hidden reserves of brutality to protect his family as they flee across rural South India. Shifting between present flight and past revelation, the film excavates the roots of caste violence and a father's buried history.

Title: Children of the Sea
Synopsis: During a sweltering summer, a lonely girl named Ruka bonds with two mysterious brothers, Umi and Sora, who were raised by dugongs and share a preternatural connection to the ocean. Their friendship draws her into an overwhelming cosmic event tied to the origins of all life, rendered through visually extraordinary, increasingly abstract animation.

Title: Dance with Me
Synopsis: After an accidental hypnosis session at a theme park, a career-driven woman discovers she cannot hear music without involuntarily breaking into song and dance, throwing her professional life into chaos. She embarks on a cross-country pursuit of the hypnotist responsible, encountering a succession of eccentric characters along the way.

Title: Dancing with the Birds
Synopsis: Narrated by Stephen Fry, this short Netflix nature documentary captures the elaborate, often comically extravagant courtship dances performed by male birds — including birds of paradise, bowerbirds, and manakins — in order to attract mates. Each species has evolved a wholly distinct performance, from optical illusions to precisely arranged galleries of coloured objects.

Title: Deadwood: The Movie
Synopsis: Set roughly ten years after the end of the original HBO series, the film reunites the residents of Deadwood as South Dakota's 1889 statehood celebrations draw both old friends and old enemies back to town, most dangerously the now-powerful Senator George Hearst. Written by David Milch, it provides a long-awaited reckoning for Al Swearengen, Seth Bullock, and the community they built.

Title: Diego Maradona
Synopsis: Drawing on over 500 hours of previously unseen private footage and home video, the documentary examines the extraordinary and turbulent years Diego Maradona spent at Napoli during the 1980s, where he became a god to an impoverished city while his personal life unravelled under pressure from the Camorra, the media, and his own appetites. Kapadia explores the painful split between the humble Diego and the mythic Maradona that the footballer himself struggled to reconcile.

Title: El Camino: A Breaking Bad Movie
Synopsis: Picking up immediately after the Breaking Bad finale, Jesse Pinkman is on the run from a massive police manhunt and must draw on whatever resources he can find to secure a new identity and escape his past. Interspersed flashbacks illuminate the psychological toll of his captivity and what survival has ultimately cost him.

Title: First Love
Synopsis: A young amateur boxer recently diagnosed with a brain tumour crosses paths with a woman ensnared in the Tokyo drug trade, and the two are thrown together into a single catastrophic night in which corrupt police officers, Yakuza factions, and Chinese gangsters pursue one another in an escalating spiral of mistaken identities and violence. Miike treats the mayhem with darkly comic energy and unexpected tenderness.

Title: Gully Boy
Synopsis: Inspired by the real Mumbai street rappers Divine and Naezy, the film follows Murad, a young man from the Dharavi slums who discovers hip-hop as a language equal to his frustrations and dreams, and begins performing despite the crushing expectations of his family and community. His journey to self-expression is complicated by class, loyalty, and the precariousness of everything around him.

Title: Horror Noire: A History of Black Horror
Synopsis: Based on Robin Means Coleman's scholarly book, the documentary traces over a century of Black representation in American horror cinema, from the racist caricatures of early Hollywood through the Blaxploitation era and the subversive work of Jordan Peele. Interviews with directors, actors, and academics examine how the genre has alternately exploited, excluded, and empowered Black voices.

Title: Invader Zim: Enter the Florpus
Director: Jhonen Vasquez, Hae Young Jung, Young Kyun Park
Synopsis: The Irken invader Zim resurfaces after a long unexplained absence with a scheme to teleport Earth directly into the flight path of his people's armada, inadvertently tearing open a catastrophic rift in space-time. His human nemesis Dib, having let himself go completely while waiting for Zim's return, must reclaim his fitness and his father's respect to stop the planet from being destroyed.

Title: Jallikattu
Synopsis: When a water buffalo escapes a Kerala slaughterhouse and rampages through a remote village in the dead of night, the entire male population turns out to recapture it, and what begins as a community effort descends into frenzied, atavistic violence. The film functions as a visceral allegory for the thin membrane between civilisation and the primal, with the animal less a villain than a mirror.

Title: Kaithi
Synopsis: A newly released prisoner, racing to meet the daughter he has never known, stumbles upon a van full of police officers incapacitated by a drug cartel's poison and finds himself coerced into becoming their unlikely protector across a single relentless night. With no phone, no support, and no weapons, he must navigate a city swarming with cartel enforcers to keep the officers alive until morning.

Title: Labyrinth of Cinema
Synopsis: Three young men who attend an all-night war-film marathon at a seaside cinema find themselves transported inside the movies, journeying through key episodes of Japanese military history in a formally riotous, deeply anti-war meditation. Obayashi completed the film while receiving terminal cancer treatment, and it stands as both his swansong and among his most passionate works.

Title: Light of My Life
Synopsis: A decade after a plague has killed nearly all women on Earth, a father shelters his young daughter by disguising her as a boy as they move cautiously through a dangerous, depopulated wilderness. The film is built around their intimate conversations and the fragile, fiercely loving bond between them, set against a world of quiet menace.

Title: Love, Antosha
Synopsis: A documentary tribute to actor Anton Yelchin, who died in a freak accident in 2016 at age 27, weaving together interviews with family, friends, and colleagues including Jennifer Lawrence and J.J. Abrams. Beyond his film career, it reveals the depth of his other artistic passions in music, photography, and writing — portrait of a young man of extraordinary creative breadth.

Title: Lupin III: The First
Synopsis: In the first fully CG-animated film in the Lupin III franchise, master thief Arsene Lupin III pursues the Bresson Diary, a mysterious WWII-era artefact that a dangerous neo-Nazi organisation will stop at nothing to obtain. Lupin must contend with both a formidable new rival and the diary's dark connection to a young woman's identity.

Title: Marighella
Synopsis: A biographical drama chronicling Carlos Marighella, the Brazilian communist intellectual who broke from the Party to found an urban guerrilla movement and wage direct armed resistance against the military dictatorship that seized power in 1964. The film tracks his transformation from political theorist to the country's most hunted man, framing him as a figure of both conviction and tragedy.

Title: On-Gaku: Our Sound
Synopsis: Three fearsome high school delinquents with zero musical background impulsively decide to form a band, and through sheer minimalist naivety — they can barely play a note — stumble accidentally into something transcendent. Drawn in deliberately rough, hand-made animation over seven years by a solo artist, the film is a deadpan and oddly moving meditation on creative spontaneity.

Title: Paddleton
Synopsis: Michael, a gentle reclusive man diagnosed with terminal cancer, and Andy, his younger equally socially awkward downstairs neighbour, embark on a road trip to obtain medication for a self-chosen death. The film observes their profound, undemonstrative friendship with quiet precision as Andy struggles to accept Michael's decision with the same dignity Michael himself brings to it.

Title: Rolling Thunder Revue: A Bob Dylan Story by Martin Scorsese
Synopsis: Scorsese blends authentic concert footage from Bob Dylan's 1975-76 Rolling Thunder Revue tour — featuring a masked, white-faced Dylan at the height of his powers — with fabricated interview segments and invented characters presented as genuine, creating an intentionally slippery portrait of an artist who has always resisted definition. The result interrogates memory, myth-making, and the nature of documentary itself.

Title: Steven Universe: The Movie
Synopsis: Two years after Steven has helped broker peace across the galaxy, a new threat arrives: Spinel, a deranged Gem who was the devoted playmate of Steven's late mother and was abandoned by her for thousands of years, now wielding a weapon capable of destroying all life on Earth. The animated musical explores themes of grief, abandonment, and the difficulty of change through a succession of original songs.

Title: Super Deluxe
Synopsis: Four interconnected stories unfold over one tumultuous night in Tamil Nadu: a transgender woman returns home to a family that rejected her, a couple discovers a dead man in their marital bed, a group of boys accidentally access a contraband VHS tape, and a devout man's faith ruptures after a violent vision. The film uses these crossing narratives to probe guilt, gender, caste, and what it means to be truly seen by another person.

Title: The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind
Synopsis: An adaptation of William Kamkwamba's memoir, set in Malawi during the catastrophic 2001 famine, in which a 13-year-old boy is forced out of school when his family can no longer pay the fees. Teaching himself engineering from a library book he is not technically permitted to borrow, he constructs a wind-powered water pump from salvaged materials that saves his village's crops.

Title: The Final Exit of the Disciples of Ascensia
Synopsis: A low-budget Canadian musical comedy following the members of a fringe New Age cult who have gathered in devoted preparation for their prophesied final night on Earth, believing a spacecraft will arrive to carry them away in a spiritual ascension. As the appointed hour approaches, the group's faith, relationships, and shared delusions are put to the test.

Title: The Legend of Hei
Synopsis: A young cat spirit named Hei, who shifts between the form of a small black cat and a child, roams freely in the forest until human development forces him to choose sides in a conflict between a radical spirit who wants to expel humanity by force and a more tempered mediator who seeks compromise. The Chinese animated film is a visually graceful exploration of belonging and the contested boundary between the human and spirit worlds.

Title: The Swallows of Kabul
Synopsis: Rendered in delicate watercolour-influenced animation, the film follows two couples whose lives intersect in Taliban-controlled Kabul: a disillusioned former intellectual whose reckless act sets tragedy in motion, and a prison warden whose deeply devout wife makes a secret, devastating sacrifice for a condemned stranger. Adapted from the novel by Yasmina Khadra, it portrays a city of beauty and terror in equal measure.

Title: Togo
Synopsis: A dramatisation of the largely uncredited 1925 Nome serum run, focusing on musher Leonhard Seppala and his veteran lead sled dog Togo, who together navigated the most gruelling and dangerous leg of the relay that carried diphtheria antitoxin across blizzard-ravaged Alaska. The film unfolds across parallel timelines to trace the unique bond between Seppala and Togo from the dog's difficult puppyhood.

Title: Waiting for the Carnival
Synopsis: A Brazilian documentary set in the Agreste region of Pernambuco, home to one of the world's largest open-air textile markets, observing workers and micro-entrepreneurs whose livelihoods are increasingly precarious as many emigrate to Portugal and other European countries in search of better wages. The film holds this economic displacement in tension with the enduring festive spirit and community bonds of the region.

Title: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker
Synopsis: The surviving Resistance faces the First Order and Palpatines return in the conclusion of the nine-film Skywalker saga in Abrams divisive but commercially massive finale.
